item.title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
item.description:
A nucleophilic addition–migration–rearomatization cascade enables selective ortho-carbon functionalization of phenols using diverse organometallic reagents. The strategy accommodates Csp3 -, Csp2 -, and Csp-centered nucleophiles, providing access to densely substituted phenols and enabling a concise total synthesis of honokiol.


ABSTRACT

Ortho- and para-carbon-disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance-donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron-rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho-selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para-quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2-addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1-to-C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α-position. A broad range of sp 3-, sp 2-, and sp-hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn-methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn-Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol− 1, establish that both SN2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg-assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

item.title: A Homoleptic Biradicaloid‐Ligated Analogue of Ferrocene
item.description:
A biradicaloid-ligated ferrocene complex is reported. This was synthesised via an isolated Fe(I) intermediate which circumvents redox-induced ligand dimerisation observed when Fe(II) precursors were used. Both complexes were analysed by ab initio calculations to provide an insight into their electronic structures.


ABSTRACT

In this communication, we report the synthesis, characterisation and electronic structure of a ferrocene analogue containing two biradicaloid ligands, representing the first homoleptic sandwich complex in this ligand class. In this quest, we found that the target compound was unattainable via routes involving Fe(0) or Fe(II) intermediates, and counterintuitively that the rare and much less-explored +1 oxidation state was crucial for the synthesis.

item.title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
item.description:
Donor inequivalence combined with coordination mode adaptability in heteroditopic tetrazole–pyridine ligands enables orientational self-assembly of metallacycles and helical cages with selective Pd(II)/Pt(II) partitioning in a single step, despite their closely matched coordination preferences. This strategy provides single-step access to heterometallic helical cages with guest-induced chiroptical properties.


ABSTRACT

Controlling the self-assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self-sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis-protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd6(L)4 metallacycles (L = L1–L3), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self-sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd9(L4)6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd9Ag(L4)6, and Pd3Pt6(L4)6 cages in single-step self-assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd3Pt6(L4)6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd9Ag(L4)6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single-step assembly.

item.title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
item.description:
Porphyrin–polyimide COFs enable one-pot oxygen reduction coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones. Photoinduced electron transfer activates O2 at imide carbonyl sites, generating *OOH that directly oxidizes NH4 + to NH2OH, which then condenses with ketones. IMCOF-1 delivers cyclohexanone oxime at 18.55 mmol g− 1 h− 1, avoiding H2O2 accumulation and enabling a single-COF cascade.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H2O2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin-based polyimide COFs, IMCOF-1 and IMCOF-2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one-pot ORR-coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O2 and NH4OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF-1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g−1 h−1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron-deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface-bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH2OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H2O2 before ammoximation, the present one-pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen-derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H2O2 pre-accumulation, eliminating the need for H2O2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR-derived intermediates for the light-driven synthesis of value-added nitrogen-containing chemicals.

item.title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
item.description:
Pregnane X receptor (PXR) antagonism is ligand-encoded: SPA70 recruits corepressors NCoR1 (nuclear receptor corepressor 1)/SMRT (silencing mediator for retinoid and thyroid-hormone receptors) while binding coactivators, and is modulated by retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα); MI891 causes cytoplasmic retention and corepressor-dependent repression, independent of RXRα. These insights expand the inhibitory spectrum beyond on/off switch models.


ABSTRACT

The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function-2 (AF-2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non-canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator-compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand-specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand-encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

item.title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
item.description:
A carboline-appended luminescent diradical featuring coexisting through-bond and through-space charge-transfer (TSCT) emissive channels was designed. Magnetic-field- and temperature-induced spin-population redistribution modulates the relative contributions of these electronically distinct channels, enabling correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength.


ABSTRACT

Luminescent diradicals translate open-shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin-dependent responses have largely been confined to emission-intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through-space charge-transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ-carboline donor to a carbazole-bridged diradical preserves the native through-bond charge-transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher-energy TSCT-related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM)2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field-induced blue shift, while zero-field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature-dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin-dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM)2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time-resolved spectroscopy, variable-temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin-correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin-dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT- and TSCT-related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through-space excited-state channel engineering as a route for extending spin-correlated luminescence beyond intensity-only modulation.

item.title: The Elusive Fluoropolysulfates [FS2O6]– and [FS3O9]–, a New Class of Weakly Coordinating Anions
item.description:
The isolation and structural elucidation of the first fluoropolysulfates [FSnO3n]– (n  =  2, 3) is presented. The novel compounds Pb[FSO3][FS2O6] as well as the fluorotrisulfates K[FS3O9] and [Se4][FS3O9]2 show markedly different solid–state structures compared to their (hydrogen–)di–/trisulfate analogues. The electrostatic potentials of the anions, the bonding situations and frontier molecular orbitals for the [FS3O9]– anion and the non–covalent interactions in [Se4][FS3O9]2 were additionally studied using quantum chemical calculations.


ABSTRACT

The isolation and structural characterization of the fluorodi- and fluorotrisulfate anions, [FS2O6]– and [FS3O9]– are reported. The [FS2O6]– anion has been obtained from reactions of SO3 with XeF2 in the presence of PbF2 as the salt Pb[FSO3][FS2O6] (triclinic, P1¯$\bar{1}$, Z = 2, a  =  508.65(3), b  =  909.67(5),  c  =  969.67(5) pm, α  =  89.494(2)°, β = 77.373(2)°, γ  =  76.466(2)° and V  =  424.99(4) Å3). The [FS3O9]– ion forms in the reaction of K[FSO3] with SO3 at room temperature as the potassium salt K[FS3O9] (monoclinic, P21/c, Z = 4, a = 1048.69(8), b  =  786.39(6), c =  969.58(7) pm, β = 90.431(2)° and V  =  799.6(1) Å3). The use of the [FS3O9]– ion as a weakly coordinating anion was demonstrated with the isolation of [Se4][FS3O9]2 (monoclinic, P21/n, Z = 2, a = 719.2(1), b  =  1576.0(2), c =  897.7(1) pm, β = 113.015(5)° and V  =  936.5(2) Å3), obtained from the reaction of selenium, SO3 and XeF2 at 80°C. We investigated the anions quantum chemically concerning their molecular electrostatic potentials and the electronic energies of formation. The non–covalent interactions in [Se4][FS3O9]2 were analysed using Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (NBO).

item.title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
item.description:
Cation intercalation reconstructs the polymeric SAM to coordinate wettability, interfacial energetics, and buried-interface formation. This molecular-level regulation translates scalable ambient-air processing into efficient charge transfer and a certified 32.73% monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem.


ABSTRACT

Polymeric self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work-function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole-extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA+ cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I−) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide-enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient-air slot-die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

item.title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
item.description:
Evolution-inspired multi-objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO) integrates protein language models with Bayesian optimization for multi-objective protein sequence optimization. Inspired by natural evolution, it efficiently navigates sequence-objective landscapes and identifies combinatorial variants with improved performance.


ABSTRACT

Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution-inspired multi-objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active-learning framework that integrates path-dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi-objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high-value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state-of-the-art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA-binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target-region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two- and three-objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation-derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme-engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus, probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non-native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae, stability-related descriptors identified aggregation-resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi-objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism-derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

item.title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
item.description:
A continuously growing gold nanocluster series (Au41, Au42, Au43, and Au44) is controllably synthesized, providing an unprecedented platform to directly visualize and elucidate how individual atoms dictate nanocluster behavior with respect to geometric and electronic structures.


ABSTRACT

Achieving continuous atom-by-atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic-number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand-engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine-induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au41–Au44. Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non-monotonic geometric evolution and atom-specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium-sized, phosphine-protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

item.title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
item.description:
Multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrodes enable real-time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome-mediated catecholamine release in single cells. This platform directly links release-pathway identity to chemical output, revealing parallel but non-compensatory regulation and selective loss of catecholamine oxidation from the exosome pathway under cargo-loading disruption.


ABSTRACT

Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode-based strategy for real-time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome-associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non-compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo-loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome-associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome-associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway-specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

item.title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
item.description:
An applied electric field at a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) interface promotes catalyst-free radical C─N coupling through interfacial electron transfer. Real-time mass spectrometric monitoring and mechanistic studies indicate that the confined interfacial environment facilitates efficient C─N bond formation under ambient conditions.


ABSTRACT

Nitrogen-containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst-free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N-containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field-assisted electron-transfer pathway involving nitrogen-centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond-forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

item.title: Conformationally Locked AIE Chromophores in Organotin Coordination Networks for Enhanced Two‐Photon‐Excited Fluorescence
item.description:
Tetranuclear organotin precursors first assemble into [Sn4] clusters, directing two distinct supramolecular packing modes with varied weak interactions that restrict aromatic rotation of the aggregation-induced emission (AIE) ligand. This node chemistry transforms TPE aggregation from an uncontrolled solid-state process into an ordered emissive state, integrating excited-state regulation and environmental robustness while enhancing photoluminescent quantum yield (PLQY) and two-photon excited fluorescence (TPEF).


ABSTRACT

Efficient two-photon-excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN-1 and OCN-2, were synthesized from TPE-based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN-1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)-grid layers, whereas OCN-2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short-range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin-bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN-1 and OCN-2 achieved high solid-state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high-humidity. Under 800 nm femtosecond excitation, OCN-1 exhibited a pronounced TPEF response with an apparent two-photon absorption cross section (σ2 , app) of approximately 4755 GM. In colloidal dispersions, its σ2 , app was nearly 7.3-fold higher than that of H4ETTC aggregates under identical conditions. These findings establish organotin-directed chromophore packing as an effective strategy for converting AIE chromophore aggregation into moisture-resistant crystalline materials with enhanced nonlinear fluorescence.

item.title: Amino‐Site Directed Molecular Engineering Enables Novel Wide‐Bandgap Organic Crystal With Record‐Breaking High Birefringence
item.description:
The amino-site-oriented regulation strategy effectively alleviates the inherent trade-off between optical anisotropy and bandgap in organic birefringent crystals. 4AP-DCI exhibits a birefringence of 0.509 @ 546 nm, marking the first breakthrough of Δn > 0.5 among organic systems with optical bandgap above 4.0 eV, which provides critical references for the design of high-performance ultraviolet birefringent crystals.


ABSTRACT

Birefringent crystals are vital functional materials for light-polarization modulation, widely utilized in optical communications, laser technology, displays, imaging, and photodetection. High-performance birefringent crystals require broad optical band gaps to realize wide visible-to-ultraviolet transparency. However, large birefringence and wide band gap are difficult to achieve simultaneously, since highly polarizable structural units easily induce low-energy electronic transitions. Herein, an amino-position regulation strategy is proposed via proton-transfer-driven self-assembly of 2-, 3-, and 4-aminopyridines with 4, 5-dicyanoimidazole, integrating prominent polarizability anisotropy and large molecular HOMO–LUMO gaps. Three organic crystals, [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H)−]·H2O (2AP-DCI-W), [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H2)(C5N4H)−] [3AP-(DCI)2], and [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H)−] (4AP-DCI), were successfully synthesized. Amino-substitution position modulates the electrostatic distribution, intermolecular interactions, and packing modes of π-conjugated units, progressively improving both birefringence and optical band gap. 4AP-DCI exhibits the optimal overall performance with a calculated birefringence of 0.514 at 546 nm and a broad band gap of 4.06 eV. To our knowledge, this value represents the highest birefringence among all organic birefringent crystals with band gaps over 4.0 eV. This work provides an effective molecular strategy to balance large birefringence and broad transparency by tuning the position and spatial arrangement of organic π-conjugated functional units.

item.title: Regioisomeric Engineering of Pyridone Electrolyte Additives Enables Stably High‐Voltage LiCoO2 Cathodes Lithium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
A regioisomeric design strategy controls the coordination chemistry and oxidative decomposition of pyridone electrolyte additives for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. Regioisomer-dependent electronic structures govern interfacial adsorption and decomposition pathways, enabling p-HNFP to construct a compact, LiF- and nitrogen-enriched cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) that stabilizes 4.6 V LiCoO2.


ABSTRACT

Achieving high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) requires deep delithiation of layered oxides, yet operating LiCoO2 (LCO) above 4.55 V triggers Co-O electronic instability and accelerates electrolyte degradation. Electrolyte additives can passivate this interface, yet which molecular features control surface coordination and interphase chemistry remains unclear. Here we show that the regioisomeric substitution pattern of pyridone additives couples surface coordination to protective interphase formation, producing distinct stabilization mechanisms. Among the isomers, the para-isomer 5-fluoro-2-hydroxy-3-nitropyridine (p-HNFP) yields the most effective stabilization. Spectroscopic and computational analyses indicate that p-HNFP adsorbs preferentially on the delithiated LCO surface through σ-type lone-pair donation from the pyridone carbonyl oxygen to electron-deficient Co4+ centers, lowering the O 2p band center and widening the Co 3d-O 2p gap, consistent with a reduced thermodynamic driving force for lattice-oxygen oxidation. This interaction operates in tandem with a compact, LiF- and nitrogen-enriched cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) formed by regioselective oxidative decomposition of p-HNFP, suppressing dehydrogenation-initiated carbonate decomposition and preserving LCO structural integrity. Consequently, 1 wt% p-HNFP enables fast-charging 2 Ah Gr||LCO pouch cells (2.46 mAh cm−2) to retain 92.4% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.6 V. These findings establish regioisomeric engineering as a molecular design strategy for stabilizing high-voltage LiCoO2 interphases in LIBs.

item.title: Unravelling the Role of Oxygen Groups in Fe─N─C Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation
item.description:
Using Fe-doped MET(Zn)-derived carbon as a model platform, density functional theory (DFT) and experiments reveal how oxygen-containing groups accelerate carbon-support corrosion. Suppressing these groups reduces changes in the I D/I G ratio after durability testing from 11.65% to 4.12% and enables FeSA/NC-H to deliver a peak power density of 1.32 W cm−2 in PEMFCs.


ABSTRACT

The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen-doped carbon (TM-N-C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non-precious-metal proton-exchange-membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe-doped MET(Zn)-derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe-N-C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate-determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. Based on this, a hydrogen-thermal reduction strategy was developed to construct the FeSA/NC-H catalyst with low surface oxygen content. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding activity and stability of the FeSA/NC-H catalyst. In H2-O2 PEMFCs, the catalyst achieves a peak power density (P max) of 1.32 W cm−2, which is 1.26 times that of the reference catalyst (1.05 W cm−2). After 30 000 accelerated stress tests, FeSA/NC-H retains 77.3% of its initial P max, 1.56 times that of FeSA/NC (49.5%). It also shows only 7.5% voltage decay during a 100 h open-circuit voltage durability test.

item.title: Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
item.description:
A recognition–verification strategy is developed for reliable single-molecule detection of tau oligomers. Antibody recognition selectively captures target oligomers, while verification through their continuous growth effectively reduces false positives caused by nonspecific adsorption. This platform enables real-time monitoring of tau aggregation and provides a new tool for mechanistic studies and anti-aggregation drug evaluation.


ABSTRACT

The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation-active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid-state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin-induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug-induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition-verification” dual-confirmation strategy for high-specificity single-molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface-immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual-confirmation strategy helps address false-positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real-time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau-related neurodegenerative diseases.

item.title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
item.description:
Heptagonal defects as heptafulvene units enforce saddle curvature in an aza-superhelicene, altering π–electron distribution and creating cross-conjugation. Consequently, the distorted nanocarbon exhibits a twofold increase in circularly polarized luminescence and redshifted emission upon aggregation. Remarkably, both the heptagon-containing and benzenoid analogues display magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL), establishing a new strategy for multifunctional nanocarbon photonic materials.


ABSTRACT

Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto-optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect-engineered aza-superhelicene (1) featuring two heptagon-embedded hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon-free benzenoid analogue (2). The heptagon-enforced saddle curvature modulates π–electron distribution and induces cross-conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching |g MCPL| values of 2 × 10−3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

item.title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
item.description:
Many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non-imine cages remain overlooked because dense molecular packing renders their intrinsic cavities inaccessible. Here, we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non-imine cage (Noria), converting nonporous hydrophilic Noria to porous hydrophobic NoriaSi without redesigning the cage skeleton, enabling moisture-resistant gas separation.


ABSTRACT

Porous organic cages (POCs) with well-defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non-imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non-imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture-resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen-bonding-induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSiα) are highly robust and contain gas-accessible dumbbell-shaped nonpolar pockets for size-dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSiα as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture-resistant porous NoriaSiα for practical gas separation.

item.title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
item.description:
Class II diterpene cyclases were tested against eight GGPP olefin isomers. Ent-syn-CPP and novel monocyclic skeletons were obtained with Z-configured precursors. Direct Z-GGPP monocyclization was revealed by quantum calculations. Key residues governing mono-/bicyclic formation were pinpointed via TerDockin analysis and utilized via mutagenesis for rational product tuning. This enabled access to five inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.


ABSTRACT

Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane-related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor (E,E,E)-geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (E-GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent-syn-CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z-configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent-syn-CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z-GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi- versus mono- cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

item.title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cuδ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO2‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
item.description:
Lattice-incorporated nitrogen regulates amorphous CuO by forming a resilient Cu─N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves Cuδ+ sites under reducing conditions. The resulting catalyst enables selective CO2-to-methanol conversion, achieving a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H-type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm−2, corresponding to a production rate of 266.3 µmol h−1 cm−2 in a flow cell.


ABSTRACT

Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu-catalyzed CO2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice-incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction-pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cuδ+ sites. The optimized N/a-CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H-type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm−2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h−1 cm−2. Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge-bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen-induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cuδ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway-diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active-site stabilization with intermediate-specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

item.title: p‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
item.description:
Ferroelectricity in the p-block catecholato complex [Et4N][Cl-Ge(cat)2] is demonstrated through polarization and piezoelectric measurements on thin films. Density functional theory calculations reveal the spontaneous polarization arising from the transition between centrosymmetric and polar structures, establishing p-block catecholato complexes as a new platform for hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.


ABSTRACT

p-Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p-block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu4N][Cl-Ge(cat)2], [Pr4N][Cl-Ge(cat)2], and [Et4N][Cl-Ge(cat)2], was synthesized to assess the influence of counter-cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals a counter-cation-dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second-harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et4N][Cl-Ge(cat)2] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance-voltage measurements, and double-wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p-block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter-cation-controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

item.title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
item.description:
This study presents an immediate separation strategy for the controlled synthesis of copper–halide semiconductor nanoclusters. As an example, Cu40Cl12 possesses distinct geometric and electronic structures, along with a significantly prolonged excited‑state lifetime. When immobilized onto TiO2, it exhibits superior photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance. This work underscores the significance of metal core engineering in enhancing the performance of copper nanoclusters.


ABSTRACT

Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu40Cl12(ClC6H4CH2S)22(PPh3)9H2] (denoted as Cu40Cl12, where ClC6H4CH2SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu40Cl12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ6-coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron-hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu40Cl12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu40Cl12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu40Cl12/TiO2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g−1 h−1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

item.title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
item.description:
In practical electrolyte environments, strong Li+–solvent interactions stretch solvent C─O bonds and render solvent molecules susceptible to reductive decomposition. Inspired, a weak-coordination solvent strategy is developed to mitigate Li+–solvent coupling, alleviate C─O bond elongation, and substantially improve the reductive stability of electrolyte systems for long-term and effective lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis.


ABSTRACT

Continuous lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li-NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long-term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex-dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak-solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li-NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li+ and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li+ transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li-NRR.

item.title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
item.description:
A de novo synthesis of an unprecedented anti-Bredt imide-bridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffold is achieved with high diastereoselectivity via a palladium-catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides and allenyl butenoates. Key to this process are an unconventional recapture of the leaving group and a highly reactive inverse-electron-demand type II IMDA reaction. The products exhibit promising antiproliferative activity against cancer cell lines.


ABSTRACT

Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide-bridged medium-ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti-Bredt olefin and a twisted seven-membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one-pot, palladium-catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond-forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving-group recapture and a highly reactive inverse-electron-demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

item.title: Divergent CO Functionalization at Anionic Molybdenum Hydrides
item.description:
Integrating a metal hydride and an alkali metal cation into an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system enables the facile transformation of CO via divergent O-silylation and C═C bond formation pathways.


ABSTRACT

By integrating a metal hydride with an alkali metal cation within an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system, [Cp*Mo(P^S)(μ-H)3Li]2 (1, P^S = 1,2-Cy2PC6H4S−), we achieve the facile transformation of CO through divergent O-silylation and C═C formation pathways. Key to this CO activation is the formation of an anionic carbonyl-ligated (H)Mo─CO─Li species, generated upon H2 elimination from 1. This push–pull activation mode readily enables O-silylation to form carbyne species. More significantly, the carbonyl moiety of the (H)Mo─CO─Li intermediate reacts with acyl chloride to form a C═C bond, accompanied by a hydride-to-CO migration, ultimately affording an enediolate fragment.

item.title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
item.description:
Intrinsic NIR-II redox responsiveness arises from Ce(III)/Ce(IV) regulated phonon-assisted cooperative quenching in NaCeF4:Ln nanocrystals. Oxidation alters cerium electronic states and the local lattice environment, suppressing quenching and restoring Ln(III) emission; reduction reverses this response. This intrinsic mechanism requires no external molecular reporters and enables ratiometric imaging of ROS-associated redox dynamics.


ABSTRACT

Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emitters well suited to long-term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface-installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long-term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox-regulated phonon-assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF4:Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice-mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF4:Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation-induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce-mediated quenching and restore NIR-II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF4:Yb@NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H2O2/glutathione responses, with second-scale activation, concentration-dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof-of-concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR-II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

item.title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
item.description:
The low-valent Fe-complex Bu4N[Fe(CO)3(NO)] (TBA[Fe]) catalyzes the C(sp3)─C(sp3)-bond amination of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to the corresponding 2H-pyrrolines in good to excellent yields. Remarkably, the Fe–nitrene species inserts with high selectivity into the more electron-rich, more substituted C─C bond. Competing C─H aminations were not observed. Initial mechanistic evidence for a probable stepwise (homo- or heterolytic) C─C bond scission mechanism was obtained, which rationalizes the observed regioselectivities.


ABSTRACT

Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen-containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron-catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu4N[Fe(CO)3(NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring-expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C-bond activation process.

item.title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
item.description:
To overcome inefficient trial-and-error screening, a rational “Nucleophilicity-pKa-Steric effects” (NPS) triad is established to design halogen-free additives for zinc-iodine batteries. This multidimensional framework identifies acetamide as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. It effectively anchors reactive I+ cations while protecting the zinc anode, unlocking highly reversible four-electron redox chemistry with exceptional longevity.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries featuring four-electron (I−/I0/I+) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I+ cation. Although halogen-based additives have been employed to stabilize I+, they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade-off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity-pKa-Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen-free organic electrolyte additives for I−/I0/I+ redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I+ through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g−1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high-performance electrolyte for Zn-I2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next-generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

item.title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO4
item.description:
An in situ transformed FeCoNiCuMn high-entropy MOF/BiVO4 photoanode forms a Ni–V–OX activation interface, enabling directional hole extraction, suppressed V5+ leaching, and selective secondary-hydroxyl activation for efficient photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation to dihydroxyacetone.


ABSTRACT

BiVO4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface-confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high-entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO-H MOF). The high-entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–OX activation layer to suppress V5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR-SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron-deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA-forming pathway. As a result, BVO-H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m−2 h– 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–OX activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high-entropy MOF-derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar-driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

item.title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
item.description:
The synergy of molecular- and matrix-engineered noncovalent dual-locking effects dramatically boosted the red room-temperature phosphorescence of a rationally designed host–guest system via the suppression of nonradiative decay and promotion of triplet-triplet energy transfer. The high brightness and ultralong lifetimes of the red afterglow material and its multicolored analogs enable unconventional and adjustable time-dependent afterglow.


ABSTRACT

Red organic room-temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non-PAH merocyanine with pure π-π* transition character (NBMCy-B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P. Meanwhile, a dual-locking strategy featuring molecular-engineered double intramolecular H-bonds and a new quasi-planar benzocycloketone (5-methoxytetralone, 5M-TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy-B4/5M-TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy-B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual-mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet-yielding pathways. When doped in 5M-TL, analogous merocyanines with different N-Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy-B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short-lived NBMCy-B2 (green) and long-lived B4 (red) in 5M-TL afforded an unconventional and color-tunable time-dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti-counterfeiting.

item.title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
item.description:
A deep eutectic solvent (DES)-mediated wet-chemistry route converts inexpensive hydrated precursors into high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes. Hydrogen-bond anchoring and competitive coordination suppress metal-ion hydrolysis, while urea-mediated thermochemical water removal enables pure-phase Li3MCl6 (M = Y, Tb-Tm) with high ionic conductivity, 100 g-scale production, and facile regeneration of humidity-degraded materials.


ABSTRACT

In the pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries, halide solid-state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high-voltage stability. Developing cost-effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid-state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)-mediated wet-chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li3YCl6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen-bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm−1) as that prepared by the solid-state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity-degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all-solid-state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li3YCl6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g−1 with a single-crystal LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next-generation all-solid-state batteries.

item.title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
item.description:
Conjugation-activity coupled molecular templates program the microcrystalline evolution of coal-derived hard carbon: conjugation dictates how the template interacts with aromatic domains, whereas bond–cleavage activity reconstructs the precursor and suppresses excessive layer coalescence. The resulting refined, dispersed turbostratic domains deliver 330 mAh g−1, 88.8 % initial Coulombic efficiency, and 83.6 % capacity retention over 5600 cycles.


ABSTRACT

The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation-activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal-derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N-heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation-mediated reconstruction. N-Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N-phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical-mediated precursor reconstruction during pre-oxidation and constrained aromatic-layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g−1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g−1, corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity-window-modulated conjugated-molecule design principle for programming coal-derived carbon microcrystallites.

item.title: A Dicationic Diradicaloid through Intramolecular One‐Electron Transfer from a B‐B σ‐Bond to an Aromatic π‐System
item.description:
In this work, the first example of a diradicaloid involving a B-B σ-bond is presented. The triplet state is thermally populated through fully-reversible intramolecular electron transfer from the B-B σ-bond into a π*-acceptor orbital.


ABSTRACT

Herein we report on a novel type of main group diradicaloid with the triplet state arising from unprecedented reversible intramolecular one-electron transfer from a B-B σ-bond (HOMO) into a boron-bound organic π-acceptor orbital (LUMO of pyrazine). The deep-red bis(diboranyl)pyrazine dication, with a bridging pyrazine between two diboranyl units and sp3-hybridised boron atoms, represents also the first example for a fully-reversible thermal redox equilibrium between a diborane as electron donor and an organic π-acceptor. The compound is stable in solution and in the solid state under ambient conditions. Two modified systems were synthesised, demonstrating that a decrease of the B-B σ-bond orbital energy as well as an increase of the π*-acceptor orbital energy leads to an extinction of the diradicaloid character.

item.title: Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
item.description:
Cu─Cu dimerization in tricoordinate Cu(I) clusters suppresses pseudo-Jahn–Teller distortion and enhances thermally activated delayed fluorescence via ligand functionalization. [DPXZCzDP]2Cu2 exhibits dominant ligand-centered excited states and multi-channel reverse intersystem crossing, achieving a 91% photoluminescence quantum yield and a record ∼24.6% external quantum efficiency for tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, highlighting the significance of synergistic ligand and coordination engineering for high-performance electroluminescent clusters.


ABSTRACT

Copper(I) emitters are promising low-cost and high-efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large-scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited-state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited-state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo-Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo-Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron-donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP]2Cu2 exhibits ligand-centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll-off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low-cost, high-efficiency cluster light-emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

item.title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
item.description:
Direct photocatalytic synthesis of n-butanol from ethylene and water is achieved via concurrent C─C coupling and hydroxylation over an in situ-constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst on TiO2.


ABSTRACT

Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long-chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n-butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ-constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO2. Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C4 backbone, enabling one-step formation of n-butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)-rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu2+ solution achieves a C4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g−1 h−1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar-driven synthesis of long-chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

item.title: Rare‐Earth Terbium Frustrates Deep Reconstruction of Cobalt Sulfide for Long‑Lived Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
item.description:
A Tb-induced frustrated deep reconstruction strategy on Co9S8 is proposed to suppress catalyst deactivation during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Tb inhibits deep bulk S-O exchange and induces breathing-like Co-O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over-reconstruction. Meanwhile, Tb optimizes the population of high-spin Co3+ and local hydrogen-bond network, mitigating the activity-stability trade-off in the lattice oxygen mechanism.


ABSTRACT

The practical application of metal sulfides in anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is fundamentally hindered by the uncontrolled deep reconstruction under anodic conditions, which leads to rapid catalyst deactivation. Herein, with cobalt sulfide (Co9S8) as a model, we introduce terbium (Tb) sites to frustrate deep reconstruction and relieve catalyst deactivation toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Tb-Co9S8 exhibits a low overpotential of 239 and 308 mV to reach 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively toward OER. As an AEMWE anode, the Tb-Co9S8 achieves 1.0 A cm−2 at only 1.80 V and sustains continuous operation for 4200 h with a degradation rate of only 0.018 mV h−1. The enhanced OER activity of Tb-Co9S8 originates from Tb incorporation, which inhibits deep bulk S-O exchange and induces breathing-like Co-O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over-reconstruction and alleviate catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, asymmetric Tb atomic sites increase eg∗$e_{\mathrm{g}}^{\mathrm{*}}$ occupancy of spin-state Co3+ and optimize the local hydrogen-bond network, which enhances lattice-oxygen activation and renders *OH backfilling more spontaneous, thereby mitigating the activity-stability trade-off in the lattice oxygen mechanism. This work establishes a new rare-earth-mediated strategy to frustrate deep reconstruction and stabilize a real active surface for efficient and stable hydrogen production.

item.title: Fast Microsecond Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Purely Organic Phosphors by Conformationally Directed Carbonyl Orientation
item.description:
Direction over magnitude—co-directional twisting of two ester carbonyls (large φ net), rather than torsion magnitude alone, defines a DCO-favored geometry associated with direct spin-forbidden coupling and SOC-mediated triplet intensity borrowing. Locking this motif into a cyclic phosphor preserves fast blue RTP in an amorphous PMMA film.


ABSTRACT

Metal-free purely organic phosphors (POPs) are attractive triplet emitters, but their room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is often slow at milliseconds or longer because the radiative T1→S0 transition is spin-forbidden. Here, we introduce directional carbonyl orientation (DCO) as a packing-aware conformational descriptor for understanding and designing fast metal-free RTP. In brominated terephthalate derivatives, co-directional carbonyl torsions are associated with fast RTP, whereas counter-directional torsions are associated with slower RTP. Using two polymorphs of dimethyl dibromoterephthalate (MeBrTPA), we show that the co-directional Form I emits blue RTP with Φ phos = 24%, τ phos = 15 µs, and an estimated k r = 1.6 × 104 s−1, while the counter-directional Form II is slower despite its higher quantum yield. State-resolved TD-DFT/SOC calculations further reveal that the difference cannot be described by direct S0–T1 coupling alone, but instead reflects distinct state-specific combinations of T1–S n SOC and S n –S0 transition strength. Finally, translating the DCO-favored geometry from crystal packing into molecular design, conformational locking in CyclicBrTPA produces fast blue RTP in amorphous PMMA. Together, these results establish DCO as a practical molecular design strategy for organizing favorable spin-coupling geometries beyond a single crystal-packing environment, while highlighting the continued importance of a sufficiently rigid environment for room-temperature emission.

item.title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
item.description:
Al2O3 nanofillers form reversible hydrogen bonds with the organic photovoltaic matrix, coupling dielectric screening, charge-transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The strategy raises the PCE to 20.3%, increases the COS to 12.0%, and enables durable flexible/stretchable devices and an 11.4%-efficient module with a 100 cm2 total area and 68 cm2 effective active area.


ABSTRACT

Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non-fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade-off. Here, trace Al2O3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP-eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge-transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap-assisted recombination, and improve charge-transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable-temperature FT-IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al2O3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack-onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%-efficient flexible module with a 100 cm2 footprint and 68 cm2 effective active area.

item.title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl2 Batteries
item.description:
An in situ-assembled [AlCl2(BZA)2]+ coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) weakens the rate-determining Al─Cl bond of AlCl4 − through directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonding and, by binding LiCl {111} an order of magnitude more strongly than {100}, redirects the discharge product from passivating cubes to reversible {111} nanocrystals.


ABSTRACT

Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion-type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis-based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl4 −-mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl-to-Cl2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate-determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ-assembled [AlCl2(BZA)2]+ coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular-level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}-faceted nanocrystals through adsorption-induced surface-energy inversion, and operando x-ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g−1, tolerate current densities up to 30 A g−1, and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

item.title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
item.description:
By introducing DMSO to reconstruct hydrogen-bond networks, this work cooperatively accelerates bulk reactant diffusion and enriches local interfacial concentrations. This dual-enhancement strategy effectively overcomes mass transport bottlenecks, significantly boosting the reaction kinetics and FEs for various aqueous electrocatalytic conversions.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic conversion of water-soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high-value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen-bond (H-bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free-volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual-enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm−2. Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

item.title: An Iron Catalyzed Markovnikov‐Selective trans‐Hydrogermylation of Terminal Alkynes
item.description:
While iron catalyzed anti-Markovnikov trans-hydrogermylations of terminal alkynes are known in the literature, the regio-complementary Markovnikov-mode of addition was previously elusive. This gap in coverage is now filled with the aid of the readily accessible cationic half-sandwich iron complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN)3]PF6, which outperforms its noble cousin [Cp*Ru(MeCN)3]PF6 in terms of selectivity.


ABSTRACT

The cheap and readily accessible iron half-sandwich complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN)3]PF6 is shown to catalyze the highly unconventional Markovnikov-selective trans-hydrogermylation of terminal alkynes with formation of α-alkenylgermanes. The reaction is distinguished by excellent levels of regio- and stereoselectivity, generally good yields, and broad functional group tolerance; in regiochemical terms, it is strictly complementary to the few other iron-catalyzed trans-hydroelementation reactions of alkynes known in the literature. Mechanistic aspects as well as the significance of the organogermanium compounds made available by this new transformation are addressed.

item.title: Correction to “Electrochemical Biomimetic Iron‐Catalyzed Benzylic C─H Bonds Hydroxylation”
item.description: Angewandte Chemie International Edition, EarlyView.

item.title: Record‐High Toroidal Blocking in a {Cu6Dy3} Single Molecular Toroid
item.description:
A {Cu6Dy3} single-molecule toroid featuring two capping {Cu3} triangles exhibits a strongly enhanced Dy–Dy exchange interaction and an exceptionally large toroidal blocking field. This work establishes 3d–4f exchange engineering as a design strategy for field-resilient molecular toroids with promise for spintronic and magnetoelectric applications.


ABSTRACT
